name: Saint Vincent de Paul
history: A Gascon farmer’s son who became a priest hoping for a comfortable living, and was converted to the service of the poor. He founded the Congregation of the Mission to preach to country people and, with Saint Louise de Marillac, the Daughters of Charity. He is the patron of all works of charity.
life: Vincent was born in 1581 at Pouy, in south-west France, and ordained young, in 1600, hoping for a good benefice. His own letters tell of capture by pirates and slavery in Tunis, though historians debate the story. As chaplain to the powerful Gondi family he came to see the spiritual neglect of the peasants on their estates. In 1617 a dying man’s confession at Folleville, and a sick family in his parish at Châtillon, turned his life around: he preached missions and gathered wealthy women into Confraternities of Charity. In 1625 he founded the Congregation of the Mission, and in 1633, with Louise de Marillac, the Daughters of Charity, sisters who served the sick in their homes and in the streets rather than behind a cloister. He cared for galley slaves, foundlings and refugees of war, and reformed the training of priests. He died in Paris in 1660.
prayerTo: Saint Vincent de Paul, you learned to see Christ in the poor and spent all your strength in serving them. Pray for all who work for the poor, the sick and the abandoned, and for me, that my charity may be practical and humble, and that I may love the poor as my masters in Christ. Amen.
penance: Give to the Society of Saint Vincent de Paul or another charity for the poor, or offer an hour of your time to someone in need.
meditation: Vincent told his sisters that to leave prayer to serve the poor is to leave God for God. Whose need might be God interrupting you today?
